name: Netcat - TCP/UDP Port Sweep (-z)
description: Netcat zero-I/O mode port scan. -z connects and immediately closes without sending data. -w sets a per-connection timeout in seconds. Faster than nmap for quick spot-checks when a full scanner is overkill or unavailable.
notes: Flags: -n no DNS, -v verbose (open/closed message), -vv more verbose, -w <sec> timeout per connection, -z zero-I/O (scan mode), -u UDP. UDP scanning is inherently unreliable — no response usually means open|filtered; an ICMP port-unreachable means closed. Use nmap -sU for reliable UDP with retries. nc -z is best for confirming a single port you already suspect is open.

recommended.note: Follow with nmap for banner grabbing and service version detection on confirmed open ports.
nmap -sU is more reliable for UDP — retries on no response and recognises ICMP unreachable.

defense.prerequisites: Network access to the target host. nc is pre-installed on most Linux distributions and macOS.
defense.why_it_works: TCP: nc completes (or attempts) a three-way handshake on each port. A SYN-ACK response means the port is open; RST means closed; no response means filtered. UDP: nc sends an empty datagram; ICMP port-unreachable means closed, no response means open|filtered. -z sends no application data, so service-level IDS rules that inspect payloads are bypassed.
defense.misconfiguration: Hosts with open ports not protected by a host-based firewall. UDP services (NTP, SNMP, DNS) that respond to any source.
defense.impact: Confirms which ports are open before running heavier scanners. UDP scanning reveals services like NTP (123) and SNMP (161) that nmap may miss on quick scans.
defense.detection: Firewall/IPS logs showing sequential connection attempts from the same source IP. SYN packets without subsequent data (zero-I/O) are a pattern EDR and network sensors can flag. IDS rules for rapid sequential port probes from a single source.
defense.artifacts: Network PCAP: SYN packets from attacker IP to target across sequential ports. Firewall deny/accept logs.
defense.prevention: Host-based firewall denying unsolicited inbound connections. Network IPS rate-limiting SYN packets per source. IDS alert on sequential port probes.
defense.evasion: -w 1 keeps connections brief, reducing window for detection. Single-port nc checks for specific services generate less alerting than a range scan. nc lacks the timing and fragmentation evasion flags nmap has.
